summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on finalizing rollout plan and canary/cutover steps. transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right good morning everyone thanks for joining our weekly POC sync, we'll focus mostly on rollout planning today and make sure cutover is clear.
[00:12] Maria Gonzalez: Yep thanks Jordan, wanted to make sure we cover the canary approach. Last week the latency looked good on the dedicated nodes but we saw a small jitter at 1k tokens, so want to understand the mitigation.
[00:28] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Right, so the jitter you saw was during the KV-cache warmup period, we expect that to stabilize after prefix caching warms up. For the canary we recommend short sessions first, and route 5% of traffic for 24 hours then ramp to 20% over 48 hours if no regressions.
[00:45] Tom Becker: 5% seems fine. How do we define regressions — latency p95 or error rate?
[00:52] Priya Shah: Good question; our suggestion is p95 latency spike > 50% baseline or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes triggers rollback, and quality regressions based on sample prompts — we'll tie those to eval sets.
[01:10] Maria Gonzalez: And about A/B testing, we want to run an A/B comparing quantized variant vs full fp16 for throughput/cost tradeoff — is that supported in the canary?
[01:21] Ethan Park (CSM): Yep we can do a canary + A/B where A is full model and B is 4-bit quantized variant; Redwood routing can split by header or user cohort.
[01:32] Leo Wang (SRE): I need specifics on how to shift traffic programmatically — is there an API or we use the console?
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Both, there's the Redwood Console for manual rollouts and an API for scripted shifts. Priya can share the API call examples in the runbook.
[01:46] Priya Shah: I'll include curl/postman examples and terraform snippets, and a step-by-step cutover checklist: pre-checks, start canary, monitor metrics, scale, ramp, finalize.
[01:58] Tom Becker: For pre-checks we need health-check endpoints and smoke traffic pattern. Can Redwood expose a synthetic load generator or do we need to run our own?
[02:07] Priya Shah: We don't run your synthetic inside your VPC but we can provide a load script and recommended request templates; for Dedicated we can run the smoke tests with you during a scheduled slot.
[02:20] Aisha Khan (Security): Quick security point — we need to verify KMS integration and where logs live. Are audit logs stored in Redwood cloud or can they be forwarded to our SIEM?
[02:30] Jordan Lee: Audit logs can be exported to your GCS/S3 or forwarded via syslog; for Private/VPC setups customers can retain logs in their cloud. We'll provide the SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[02:42] Aisha Khan: Also SAML/SSO and RBAC — we need the exact roles Redwood expects and how service accounts are mapped.
[02:49] Priya Shah: We'll include the SSO mappings and recommended RBAC roles in the runbook; many customers map "engineer" to read/write and "sre" to ops role.
[02:58] Maria Gonzalez: On monitoring, can you share the Redwood Console dashboard templates? We want token-level cost and latency per route visible.
[03:06] Jordan Lee: Yes, I'll share the dashboard link and a JSON export you can import. Dashboards will include p50/p95/p99, errors, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and failing prompt samples.
[03:18] Leo Wang: Alerts — what thresholds do you recommend for paging the SRE team?
[03:23] Priya Shah: For production we recommend p95 > 300ms or error rate > 0.5% for immediate page; for canary you can be more permissive but still have automated rollbacks for big regressions.
[03:35] Tom Becker: Cutover timing — we prefer midnight PST on a Sunday; what's Redwood's typical blackout and SLA expectations?
[03:42] Jordan Lee: Midnight Sunday is fine. For Dedicated we'll provision buffer capacity and we recommend a maintenance window of 2-4 hours for the full cutover, with canary starting 24-48 hours before full cutover.
[03:53] Maria Gonzalez: If the canary fails, what's the rollback process? Automated or manual?
[03:58] Priya Shah: We support automated rollback policies based on the thresholds we discussed; usually customers opt for automated rollback to last stable model variant plus a manual post-mortem.
[04:07] Aisha Khan: About encryption at rest — when we use our KMS keys does Redwood ever have access to unwrapped keys?
[04:13] Jordan Lee: No — for Private deployments with customer-managed KMS Redwood never has access to unwrapped keys; for Hosted we use customer-managed keys via a rotateable KMS integration where Redwood cannot export raw key material. We'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[04:24] Maria Gonzalez: Great. A couple practical asks: share the canary runbook, the dashboard export, and a short checklist for SREs to perform the load test.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Agreed — action items noted. Priya will draft runbook and load scripts.
[04:38] Ethan Park: Also we'll share a small sample of production prompts for quality checks — Maria will scrub PII before sharing.
[04:44] Maria Gonzalez: Yes will scrub and share by end of week.
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Any other risks? Tom?
[04:50] Tom Becker: Firewall egress rules — we need the exact IP ranges for Redwood endpoints during the canary and cutover, please include in the doc.
[04:58] Priya Shah: I'll include IP ranges and hostname FQDNs and recommended keepalives.
[05:04] Jordan Lee: Ok wrapping up — to recap: Redwood to deliver runbook, dashboard export, API examples, load scripts; Acme to confirm windows, provide scrubbed prompts, and security details. Next sync same time next week unless we need an emergency call during canary.
[05:20] Maria Gonzalez: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[05:27] [meeting ends]
